channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise improved gait, disability, and trunk repositioning more than treadmill exercise alone in chronic low back pain patients (n=45).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In older adults (≥60 yrs) with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears (MIRCTs), 95-97% achieved minimal clinically important difference after 12 weeks of nonoperative treatment, sustained to 4 years; longer symptom duration and smoking were associated with worse function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: In chronic stroke patients (n=60), sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating EMG-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG) combined with conventional therapy improved upper-limb function, spasticity, and strength significantly more than conventional therapy alone, with no difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: Adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) provided no clinically important additional improvements in pain intensity (MD -0.4 points), disability (MD -0.7 points), or circulating PGE2 concentrations compared to sham PBMT plus MCE in 148 adults with chronic non-specific low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series study of 100 patients after quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction found that early postoperative limb symmetry index (LSI) scores, particularly 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI, independently predicted 2-year patient-reported outcomes (IKDC and Lysholm scores). Patients achieving IKDC PASS generally attained a 60% to 70% LSI score by 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=75) on post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome found that both high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone. HILT demonstrated superior electrophysiological (ulnar motor nerve conduction velocity, CMAP amplitudes) and functional (DASH scores) outcomes compared to ESWT, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes Hands-On Data Acquisition and Analysis (HODA-A) as a framework for conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal examination as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process, rather than isolated manual techniques.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of functional inspiratory muscle training on diaphragm function and core stabilisation in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A 10-week multicomponent functional inspiratory muscle training (F-IMT) program significantly improved diaphragm thickness (adjusted difference, 2.434 mm; 95% CI, 1.714 to 3.261; P < .001) and mobility, pain, respiratory muscle strength, and core stabilization in 40 CNSLBP patients compared to thoracic expansion exercises.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Credibility and strength of evidence for exercise, nutritional, and combined interventions on muscle function and physical performance in older adults: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
item.description: An umbrella review of 28 meta-analyses of RCTs found the most consistently supported evidence for exercise-based interventions, particularly for fall-related outcomes, in older adults. Nutrition-only interventions showed modest benefits for muscle mass in vulnerable populations, and combined interventions improved some strength and functional outcomes.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (1177 participants) found that chronic physical exercise training significantly improved the metabolic cost of walking (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) in healthy adults, with smaller non-significant effects in stroke patients, supporting its role in improving walking economy.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Modality-specific, deficit-targeted exercise prescriptions for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 61 RCTs (3706 participants) found that multicomponent training with resistance training provided the most comprehensive benefits for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty. Elastic band resistance training was most effective for handgrip strength (MD 1.95 kg, 95% CI 1.13 to 2.76, moderate certainty).
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Efficacy of physiotherapy in reducing pain in subjects with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review with network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 25 RCTs (1,540 people) found that manual therapy and therapeutic exercise are effective for reducing pain in temporomandibular disorders (TMDs), with multimodal treatments, particularly the combination of dry needling and manual therapy, appearing most effective.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 was significantly associated with successful return to sport (78.3% achieved RTS) after patellar stabilization surgery, with an odds ratio of 3.56 (95% CI, 1.10-11.51; P = .033).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A 6-month supervised telerehabilitation program combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release significantly improved fibromyalgia impact (partial η²=0.132), sleep quality (partial η²=0.129), depressive symptoms (partial η²=0.129), and perceived stress (partial η²=0.065) in 68 adults with fibromyalgia.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Barriers and Facilitators Influencing Physiotherapists' Adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines and Return to Sport Criteria after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Qualitative Study in Austria.
item.description: A qualitative study explored barriers and facilitators influencing Austrian physiotherapists' adherence to CPGs and return to sport criteria after ACL reconstruction. Key barriers included limited guideline usability, patient expectations, resource limitations, and interprofessional misalignment, while facilitators included structured guidelines and professional development.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sex- and age-specific normative values for lower-limb field tests in elite TeamGym gymnasts.
item.description: This cross-sectional study established sex- and age-specific normative values for lower-limb functional performance in 216 elite junior and senior TeamGym gymnasts, finding significant sex × age-group interactions for hop for distance and side-hop performance, with senior males outperforming junior males across all hop outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Do treatment parameters of dry needling influence its effect on pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis (n=71 comparisons) found no dose-response relationship between dry needling parameters (sessions, muscles, twitch responses) and neck pain reduction, citing high heterogeneity and incomplete reporting.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: This qualitative study, involving 15 adolescents with low back pain in four focus groups, found that effective pain neuroscience education requires back-specific, practical, trustworthy, and engaging content tailored to young people's preferences, highlighting the importance of co-design.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A multimodal non-fatiguing recovery strategy improves neuromuscular restoration and attenuates inflammatory and oxidative stress responses following a standardized football match: a randomized crossover study
item.description: A randomized crossover study (n=20 male semi-professional football players) found that a modern multimodal non-fatiguing recovery strategy (very low-intensity cycling, foam rolling, percussive therapy) significantly improved neuromuscular restoration and attenuated inflammatory/oxidative stress markers post-match compared to passive recovery, with outcome-specific differences from traditional active recovery.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Return to Competition and Career Sustainability After Primary ACL Reconstruction in Football: A Nationwide Cohort Study of Long-Term Participation
item.description: A decade-long nationwide cohort study of 10,836 Swedish football players found that 58.5% achieved return to competition (RTC) after primary ACLR, but long-term participation was often limited (median 31 matches over 3 seasons) and strongly associated with pre-injury competitive level and sex.
item.author: Sports Medicine
